children: Daiichi Life's offer for Challenger, valuing the annuities giant at $5.7 bln, is one of five new or updated deals Down Under. Waste management, plumbing, coal and car leasing round out the tie-ups. For all the AI hype, established industries are bankers' bread and butter.
Full view will be published shortly.
Follow Antony Currie on Bluesky and LinkedIn.

Daiichi Life's Australian business, TAL Daiichi Life Australia, has offered to buy the 79.5% of Challenger it doesn't already own in a deal that values the Australian annuity provider's equity at A$8.1 billion ($5.65 billion), the target revealed in a regulatory filing on October 19. The offer represents a premium of almost 20% to Challenger shares' closing price on October 16.

Also on October 19, New Hope said it would buy the 74% it doesn't already hold of rival, unlisted coal miner Malabar Resources, in a deal valuing its equity at A$1.8 billion ($1.26 billion). New Hope will issue shares to Malabar investors to fund the transaction.

Several other already announced transactions also progressed on October 19: private equity firm EQT and waste management company Cleanaway agreed to a deal that values the latter's enterprise at A$9.3 billion ($6.47 billion); SG Fleet, which is wholly owned by buyout shop Pacific Equity Partners, won the battle to take fleet-management rival FleetPartners private at an equity valuation of A$1.13 billion ($789 million); and the go-shop period for Reliance Worldwide has ended, leaving Brookfield's A$4.1 billion ($2.86 billion) offer a month ago for the plumbing group's enterprise as the only one standing.
